nota: Words of this language that look borrowed from another language but do not exist there with that meaning, grouped by the language they imitate.

parole.significato: Meaningless activity engaged in just for show; deceptive nonsense.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, possibly coined by Damon Runyon.

parole.significato: Having, feeling or showing compassion (to or toward someone).
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, derived from a pseudo-Latin form of French compassionné, past participle of compassionner (“to feel sorry for”). By surface analysis, compassion + -ate.

parole.significato: A fit of anger or panic; conniption fit.
parole.testo: Since 1833, from American English. Unknown origin, possibly a fanciful alteration of corruption, or maybe related to captious. Alternatively an arbitrary pseudo-Latinism coinage.

parole.significato: half and half (mixture of ale and porter, or similar)
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, derived from reduplication of Latin dimidium (“half”) with -que (“and”) as a humorous English-to-Latin calque of half and half, once used by students.

parole.significato: A gadget, device, or object whose name is either unknown, forgotten, or omitted for the purpose of humor.
parole.testo: Probably of multiple origins. Partially a borrowing from Dutch dinges (“thingamajig, thingy; whatshisname, whatshername”), ding (“thing”). Probably also partially a borrowing from Afrikaans in view of

parole.significato: A person with poor judgment and taste; a foolish or silly person.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, possibly an alteration of earlier goofus (first attested in the 1920s) due to influence from Scots doof (“simpleton”). Scots doof is derived from Low German doof (“deaf”, with a secon

parole.significato: A silly or foolish person; a dork.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, derived from dog Latin dorkus, a facetious back-formation from English dork.

parole.significato: The action of erasing; deletion; obliteration.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, derived from ērādō (“to erase”) + -tūra (“abstract noun suffix”), equivalent to erase + -ure.

parole.significato: that which is; an entity, a being, an existent
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, coined by Ralph Manheim in his 1959 English translation of Martin Heidegger’s Einführung in die Metaphysik to render German Seiendes (as distinct from Sein) on the basis of *essens, a

parole.significato: outward, outwards.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, based upon Latin extra- (“outside, beyond”) under the influence of the distinction between Latin intro- (“inwards”) and intra- (“inside, within”). Formations in English are mostly lim

parole.significato: The act or habit of describing or regarding something as unimportant, of having no value or being worthless.
parole.testo: From Latin floccus (“a wisp”) + naucum (“a trifle”) + nihilum (“nothing”) + pilus (“a hair”) + -fication. A pseudo-Latinism orignating as a jocular coinage, apparently by pupils at Eton College, combi

parole.significato: omnium-gatherum
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, derived from gather + Latin -um.

parole.significato: Synonym of doofus.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, derived from goof + Latin -us, possibly taking its ending from ignoramus.

parole.significato: To play a trick on, to trick (someone); to hoax; to cheat.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, derived from ellipsis of hocus-pocus. The verb is from the noun.

parole.significato: A phrase used (by a stage magician, etc.) as a magical incantation to bring about some change: abracadabra, hey presto.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism. The interjection and noun are derived from pseudo-Latin magical incantations used by conjurers (formerly called “jugglers”) such as “hocus pocus, tontus talontus, vade celeriter jubeo

parole.significato: All together; entirely; without modification.
parole.testo: Reduplication; further etymology unknown. Possibly of Ancient Greek origin, from ὅλος (hólos, “whole”) and βόλος (bólos, “a throw with a casting net”) or βῶλος (bôlos, “lump”). Alternatively, a pseudo

parole.significato: In computer simulation or in virtual reality.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, derived from in and silicon (from Latin silex (“flint, pebble, stone; crag, rock”)) + Latin -ō, by analogy with English in vitro (“in glass, referring to an experiment conducted in a

parole.significato: A person who loves or admires underdogs.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, derived from infra- + canine + -phile. An early twentieth-century coinage by American writer Christopher Morley.

parole.significato: A dummy text used as a placeholder in printing and website design to simplify the layout process, especially the usual…
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, derived from a clipping of dolōrem ipsum (“pain itself”) from Cicero's 45 B.C.E. De Fīnibus Bonōrum et Malōrum adopted by the mid-1960s to assist with artistic text layout.

parole.significato: A miscellaneous mixture.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, a reduplication derived from mix + Latin -um and gather + Latin -um.

parole.significato: An invalid argument, which has this form
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, derived from modus (“mode”) + English moron, literally “moron mode”, by analogy with modus ponens and modus tollens.

parole.significato: Don't let the bastards grind you down
parole.testo: Humorous pseudo-Latinism, from noli (“do not permit”) [singular] and illegitimi (“bastards”) [in the wrong grammatical case] and from the Latinate brand name Carborundum for a silicon carbide abrasive

parole.significato: omnium-gatherum
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, derived from omni- + gather + Latin -um.

parole.significato: Synonym of red-baiting.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, derived from reductio ad absurdum by analogy with reductio ad Hitlerum.

parole.significato: Serving or tending to seclude (oneself); affecting seclusion.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, derived from *sēclūsīvus, a combination of sēclūdō (“to seclude”) + -īvus (“-ive”), whence the native Latin sēclūsus. Equivalent to seclude + -ive.

parole.significato: Seriousness, especially self-seriousness.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, derived from serious + -itude, with the spelling changed to suggest a pseudo-Latin derivation.

parole.significato: A female demon which comes to men, especially monks, in their dreams to seduce them and have sexual intercourse, drawin…
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, derived from alteration of Late Latin succuba (“strumpet, especially a mythological fiend in female form who has intercourse with men in their sleep”) based on incubus in Middle Engli

parole.significato: According to the rules of an old drinking game in which the drinker upturned the empty cup and had to drink more if the…
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism from super- + naculum, nagulum, Latinized form of German Nagel, intended to mean “upon the nail”, after the German phrase auf den Nagel (trinken).

parole.significato: Completely; unreservedly.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, a reduplication derived from Latin tōtus (“whole”) + porcus (“hog”); translated as whole hog.

parole.significato: trinkum-trankum
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, derived from ellipsis of trinkum-trankum.

parole.significato: trinkum-trankum
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, derived from trinket + Latin -um.

parole.significato: A trinket.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, derived from a humorous reduplication of trinket with Latin -um.

parole.significato: Relating to the vermis
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, from a supposed *vermalis, whereas Latin vermiculātus. From vermis + -al.

parole.significato: A coupon-based system of hitchhiking that operated in communist Poland from the 1950s until the 1990s.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Polish autostop, from French auto-stop, and this a pseudo-anglicism, from auto- (relating to cars) + stop (hitchiking).

parole.significato: a genre of fictional media originating in Japan that features homoerotic relationships between male characters; yaoi
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese ボーイズラブ (bōizu rabu), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from boys + love.

parole.significato: A type of hotel with a number of very small "rooms" (capsules).
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese カプセルホテル (kapuseru hoteru), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from capsule + hotel.

parole.significato: A small café or restaurant typically selling light refreshments along with coffee-based drinks.
parole.testo: From coffee + shop. Sense 2 is from Dutch coffeeshop, a pseudo-anglicism of this term.

parole.significato: The activity of taking part in a dance.
parole.testo: From dance + -ing. The sense "dance club" is from French dancing, a pseudo-anglicism derived from English dance + -ing.

parole.significato: waste bin, trash can
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese ダストボックス (dasutobokkusu), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from dust + box.

parole.significato: A style of lure fishing specifically targeting squid (and occasionally cuttlefish) using a specialized wooden or plasti…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese エギング (egingu), a Wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism), derived from 餌木 (egi) + -ing.

parole.significato: A short scene or illustration used to begin and end a commercial break in a Japanese television program.
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese アイキャッチ (aikyatchi), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from eye + catch.

parole.significato: A Family Computer (chiefly those available within Japan).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese ファミコン (famikon), a syllabic abbreviation of ファミリーコンピューター (famirīkonpyūtā), a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from family + computer.

parole.significato: Elements added to a television program or similar entertainment that appeal to avid fans but are of little interest to…
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese ファンサービス (fansābisu), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from fan + service.

parole.significato: A genre of Japanese media focusing on romantic and/or sexual relationships between female characters.
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese ガールズラブ (gāruzu rabu), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from girls + love.

parole.significato: Something that one owns, especially stocks and bonds.
parole.testo: From hold + -ing. The sense "holding company" is from Russian холдинг (xolding), a pseudo-anglicism derived from an ellipsis of holding company.

parole.significato: Synonym of freeze pop, frozen fruit juice or flavored ice in a tube.
parole.testo: Calque of Japanese アイスキャンディー (aisukyandī, literally “ice candy”), a Wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism), derived from ice + candy.

parole.significato: A Japanese novel primarily targeting young adults, typically illustrated (in an anime/manga style) and containing not m…
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese ライトノベル (raito noberu), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from light + novel.

parole.significato: A fashion style originating in Japan, based on Victorian and Edwardian clothing styles, and having a cute aesthetic.
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese ロリータファッション (rorīta fasshon), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from Lolita + fashion.

parole.significato: A short-stay hotel found in Japan and elsewhere, operated primarily for the purpose of allowing lovers privacy to have…
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese ラブホテル (rabu hoteru), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from love + hotel. The term probably makes reference to the rotating sign of the Hotel Lov

parole.significato: A style of light-tackle saltwater angling originating in Japan, specifically targeting rockfish using small artificial…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese メバリング (mebaringu), a Wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism), derived from 鮴 (mebaru) + -ing.

parole.significato: The replaying of something previously recorded, especially sound or moving images.
parole.testo: From play + back. Sense 2 is from French playback, a pseudo-anglicism of this term.

parole.significato: A fictional creature from the universe of the Pokémon franchise.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese ポケットモンスター (Poketto Monsutā), itself from English pocket + monster.

parole.significato: A place believed to contain sacred power.
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese パワースポット (pawā supotto), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from power + spot.

parole.significato: A collectable item that gives the player some benefit.
parole.testo: Calque of Japanese パワーアップ (pawā-appu), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from power + up.

parole.significato: An employee, a worker; now especially a Japanese white-collar worker who works long hours yet has an insignificant posi…
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese サラリーマン (sararīman), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from salary + man.

parole.significato: Bonding through physical (touch, skin-to-skin) contact; particularly between family members, relatives and loved ones.
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese スキンシップ (sukinshippu), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from English skin + -ship, or as a blend from English skin + kinship. It is first recorde

parole.significato: A variant of tennis, developed in Japan, differing in the tennis ball used, from regular tennis (lawn tennis), having a…
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese ソフトテニス (sofuto tenisu), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from soft + tenis.

parole.significato: A video game genre that emphasizes scarcity of resources (such as health or ammunition refills) in a dangerous setting…
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese サバイバルホラー (sabaibaru horā), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from survival + horror.

parole.significato: A yoshoku dish from Okinawa, mainly consisting of ground beef on a bed of rice.
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching from Japanese タコライス (takoraisu), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from taco + rice.

parole.significato: A walkie-talkie.
parole.testo: Borrowed from French talkie-walkie, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from an inversion of English walkie-talkie.

parole.significato: A French tram driver.
parole.testo: Borrowed from French wattman, a pseudo-anglicism derived from watt + -man.

parole.significato: An agente provocatrice.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Gallicism, derived from agente + provocateur + -euse, as the French female equivalent of agent provocateur is agente provocatrice.

parole.significato: A female amateur.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Gallicism, from amateur + -euse (the French equivalent is amatrice).

parole.significato: One who engages in arbitrage, such as a financial broker or an investment bank.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Gallicism, from arbitrage + French -eur (the French term is arbitragiste).

parole.significato: A female arbitrageur.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Gallicism, from arbitrage + -euse, by analogy with arbitrageur.

parole.significato: Excellent; wonderful.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Gallicism, derived from French bon (“good”) + toujours (“always”); literally, “always good”.

parole.significato: Coffee with brandy, sometimes served with spices, cream, etc.; (countable) a serving of this beverage.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Gallicism (formed within English), from café (“coffee”), with postpositive (as usual in French) royale f, royal m (“royal”). Although café is masculine, the feminine form royale is used.

parole.significato: Dated spelling of diskette.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Gallicism, derived from disquette, corresponding to diskette.

parole.significato: A female dominant in a sadomasochistic relationship.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Gallicism, derived from dom + French -e (feminine suffix). The correct word in French is dominatrice.

parole.significato: An early form of battery-powered motorized wheelchair or slow-speed cart, typically featuring a two-person bench seat e…
parole.testo: Pseudo-Gallicism, from French électrique (“electric”) + -ette (a playful, vintage suffix inspired by the French-sounding names). Invented by Clyde H. Osborn; beginning in 1915, these carts were manufa

parole.significato: A female science fiction fan.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Gallicism, derived from fan + French -e (feminine suffix).

parole.significato: A body piercing consisting of an adornment attached to the lip.
parole.testo: From Latin labrum (“lip”) + -et; modelled on anklet, bracelet, etc. Sometimes incorrectly assumed to be of French origin. Pronounced in the fasion industry as /lɒˈbreɪ/ (pseudo-Gallicism).

parole.significato: Meek, timid; lacking character or effectiveness.
parole.testo: Named after Caspar Milquetoast, a character from the comic strip The Timid Soul, created by American cartoonist Harold Tucker Webster (1885–1952) and first published in 1924; the character was named a

parole.significato: A pseudonym used in online communications; a handle.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Gallicism, derived from nom (“name”) + de (“of”) + clavier (“keyboard”), by analogy with nom de plume.

parole.significato: A pen name or pseudonym.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Gallicism, derived from nom (“name”) + de (“of”) + plume (“feather”), by analogy with the borrowed nom de guerre.

parole.significato: A pseudonym used when publishing on the World Wide Web.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Gallicism, derived from nom (“name”) + de (“of”) + Web, by analogy with nom de guerre.

parole.significato: A soft, non-matured, Indian cheese.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani پَنِیر / पनीर (panīr), from Classical Persian پَنِیر (panīr). Sometimes pronounced as /pæˈnɪə(r)/, /pɑːˈnɪə(r)/ (pseudo-Gallicism).

parole.significato: A waiter at a restaurant who offers to grind pepper onto customers' meals at the table.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Gallicism, derived from pepper + -ier, along the lines of sommelier.

parole.significato: A female provocateur.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Gallicism, derived from provocateur + -euse, as the French female equivalent of provocateur is provocatrice.

parole.significato: A phrase that has a single, often bawdy, meaning and is lacking in subtlety or cleverness.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Gallicism. Based on double entendre.

parole.significato: Too much of a good thing.
parole.testo: A pseudo-Gallicism derived from toujours + perdrix, literally “always partridge”. The phrase is not used in French.

parole.significato: A phrase that has three meanings, especially where some meanings are innocent and literal, the other(s) risqué, bawdy,…
parole.testo: Pseudo-Gallicism. Based on double entendre.

parole.significato: An intensifier.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Hispanism, possibly from a confusion of Spanish -mente (adverbial suffix) with mundo (“world”). Popularized by the character Fonzie on the sitcom Happy Days.

parole.significato: asshole
parole.testo: Pseudo-Hispanism, derived from English asshole + -io (“noun-forming suffix”).

parole.significato: A carwasher, especially one who has immigrated to the United States from a Latin American country.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Hispanism, derived from carwasher + Spanish -ero.

parole.significato: Not good; no good; bad.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Hispanism, derived from no + bueno, a calque of no good. The closest equivalent to the adjective in Spanish is no estar bien (literally, “to not be good”); however it is a phrase rather than an

parole.significato: no more
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish no más (“only, just”). Its use as an interjection is a pseudo-Hispanism derived from an English-to-Spanish calque of no more.

parole.significato: A watermelon.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Hispanism, derived from misconstruction of Spanish sandía (“watermelon”) as a diminutive formation in -illa (feminine diminutive suffix).

parole.significato: The inherent properties of a device which affect the way it is used by individuals across cultures.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Germanism, derived from Apparat (“apparatus, device, machine”) + Geist (“spirit”). Perhaps influenced by zeitgeist. Coined by American communications academic James E. Katz.

parole.significato: The flashing lights on an electronic device such as a modem, router, or network hub (originally the front-panel lights…
parole.testo: Pseudo-Germanism from blink and lights; see the Wikipedia article for history.

parole.significato: To attack quickly or suddenly, as by an air raid or similar action.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Germanism, derived from a clipping of blitzkrieg, from German Blitzkrieg (literally “lightning war”). The German word Blitz (“lightning”) lacks the "sudden attack" senses that the English word

parole.significato: An inexplicable urge to push people away, even close friends.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Germanism, derived from Mauer (“wall”) + Bauer (“builder”) + Traurigkeit (“sorrow”). Coined by American author and neologist John Koenig, creator of The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows.

parole.significato: A specifically male barista.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Italianism, derived from barista (“bartender”), the -a having been interpreted as the Italian feminine singular ending -a, and then substituted with the masculine singular ending -o to specify

parole.significato: A braggart.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Italianism, coined after Braggadocchio, a boastful character in Edmund Spenser's The Faerie Queene (1590).

parole.significato: Used to express a personal philosophy of fatalism and acceptance of the future.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Italianism; first constructed in the 16th century for English heraldic mottos, and notably quoted as che sera sera by Christopher Marlowe in his 1604 play Doctor Faustus (Act 1, Scene 1). From

parole.significato: (archaic) third-person singular simple present indicative of may.
parole.testo: Pseudo-loan from Middle English, derived from might + -eth, an incorrect application of the archaic marker of the third-person singular present tense (-eth) to the present tense form of the verb may.

parole.significato: An American dog breed of the bulldog type.
parole.testo: Pseudo-loan from Middle English, derived from olde + English + bulldog + -e (archaizing suffix), with "bulldog" respelled based on Middle English dogge.

parole.significato: A member of a fictional race of small humanoids with shaggy hair and hairy feet.
parole.testo: Coined in its current sense by J. R. R. Tolkien in the 1930s, featured in the novels The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings. Jocularly etymologized by him as from a hypothetical Old English *holbytla (l

parole.significato: A universal solvent sought by the alchemists.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Late Latin alcahest, apparently coined by Paracelsus as a pseudo-Arabism.

parole.significato: An alert chime sampled from a xylophone, used by Apple Inc. computers.
parole.testo: Coined by Apple employee Jim Reekes in 1991, as a faux-Japanese word, that in fact was a phonetic rendering of so sue me, in reference to an ongoing lawsuit with Apple Corps over use of musical chimes

parole.significato: Mimicking Chinese, Korean, Thai or other East or Southeast Asian speech.
parole.testo: Pseudo-loan from Chinese. Onomatopoeic, originally representing characteristic syllables of Chinese, such as Mandarin's qing and chong, Cantonese's cing¹ and cong¹, Hokkien's chheng and chhong, etc.,
